rewrites.title: Ordering of AP-1 binding and epigenetic marks with synthetic recruitment
rewrites.description: At AP-1-dependent loci, map H3K27ac, H3K4me1, and DNA methylation over time after stimulus, and use CRISPR motif mutation or transient dCas9-based forced AP-1 recruitment to test whether AP-1 binding is necessary and sufficient to establish enhancer marks that outlast its presence. Marks that persist after AP-1 removal would indicate AP-1 initiates memory that is passed to chromatin, whereas persistent AP-1 occupancy itself would indicate AP-1 is the maintained state.

rewrites.title: Pulse-duration and frequency stimulation with washout
rewrites.description: Deliver defined stimulus pulses varying in amplitude, duration, and spacing, and track AP-1 reporter dynamics and chromatin accessibility for hours to days after washout. Fit linear and nonlinear state-space models to estimate decay time constants and test whether the system retains a state after input removal, and test whether a prior pulse alters the response to a later one (priming), which would indicate memory beyond the stimulus.

rewrites.title: Transient stimulus and delayed re-challenge with chromatin profiling
rewrites.description: Expose cells to a defined stimulus (e.g., TNF, serum, or wounding), allow rest until AP-1 (FOS/JUN) levels return to baseline, then re-stimulate and compare transcription and ATAC-seq accessibility with naive cells. Test whether AP-1 motif-containing enhancers stay open and whether primed genes respond faster or more strongly.

rewrites.title: Single-cell multiome and live-cell reporting of AP-1 dynamics and heritability
rewrites.description: Combine single-cell RNA+ATAC with live imaging of fluorescent AP-1 activity reporters (or endogenously tagged FOS/JUN) and lineage tracing to follow primed cells through divisions. Inheritance of AP-1 state and accessibility in daughter cells, and correlation between a cell's past AP-1 activity and its later response, would show whether memory is cell-autonomous and mitotically stable.

rewrites.title: Histone mark and SWI/SNF (BAF) dependence at AP-1 sites
rewrites.description: Measure H3K27ac, H3K4me1, and BAF occupancy at AP-1 motif-containing enhancers before, during, and after stimulation. Use BAF inhibitors or enhancer motif mutation/dCas9 editing to test whether these marks and AP-1-driven chromatin opening are necessary and sufficient for persistence.

rewrites.title: Acute degron-based AP-1 depletion at different time points
rewrites.description: Use dTAG/auxin-inducible degradation of FOS or JUN, or a dominant-negative (A-FOS), to remove AP-1 either during the priming stimulus or after it has ended. If depletion after priming erases the enhanced secondary response, AP-1 is needed to maintain memory; if only depletion during priming matters, AP-1 is needed for initiation but not maintenance.

rewrites.title: Acute AP-1 degradation after priming
rewrites.description: Use inducible degradation (dTAG/AID) or dominant-negative A-FOS either during priming or after the stimulus has ended. If the memory response persists when AP-1 is removed after priming, AP-1 is only an initiator; if it is lost, AP-1 is needed to maintain memory.

rewrites.title: Single-cell multiome tracking of memory-state heterogeneity
rewrites.description: Use scRNA+ATAC with lineage barcoding to determine whether AP-1 motif accessibility and target-gene expression define stable, heritable cell states that persist through cell divisions and predict future responsiveness.

rewrites.title: Transient pulse followed by time course of chromatin accessibility and AP-1 occupancy
rewrites.description: Give a defined stimulus pulse (e.g., TPA or a cytokine), wash it out, and run ATAC-seq and CUT&RUN for JUN/FOS and H3K27ac over days to weeks. AP-1 motif-enriched sites that stay accessible after AP-1 levels return to baseline would indicate AP-1 left a lasting epigenetic change.

rewrites.title: Single-cell multiome linking AP-1 motif accessibility to response history
rewrites.description: Run paired scRNA/scATAC (or lineage-barcoded clones) on primed and naive populations, before and after re-stimulation. Test whether cells with persistent AP-1 motif accessibility, inferred by chromVAR or footprinting, respond faster or more strongly, and whether the state is inherited by sister cells through division.

rewrites.title: AP-1 memory across quiescence and division
rewrites.description: Prime cells, then place them in quiescence (serum starvation or contact inhibition) or let them go through multiple cell cycles, for days to weeks without AP-1 activity (monitored with live AP-1 reporters). Re-challenge and test whether primed loci retain a faster, stronger response, and whether mitotic bookmarking by AP-1 (live-cell imaging, mitotic-chromosome ChIP) explains persistence, using degron removal of AP-1 during the dormant period as a causal control.

rewrites.title: Targeted epigenome editing of AP-1-dependent memory loci
rewrites.description: Use dCas9-based tools (CRISPRi/KRAB) or base-editing motif mutation at individual AP-1-bound enhancers that stay open after stimulation, and test the effect on faster or stronger reinduction of the nearby gene. Locus-specific perturbation shows which sites are necessary and sufficient, and whether memory is cis-encoded or depends on global AP-1 levels.

rewrites.title: Longitudinal ATAC-seq/CUT&RUN of AP-1 occupancy after transient stimulus
rewrites.description: Profile chromatin accessibility and FOS/JUN binding before, during, and long after a transient stimulus (e.g., injury, inflammation, or stress). Test whether AP-1-dependent accessible sites persist after the stimulus is withdrawn and AP-1 protein has returned to baseline.

rewrites.title: Motif-mutation and dCas9 perturbation of AP-1 sites at memory loci
rewrites.description: At candidate memory enhancers, use CRISPR base editing to mutate AP-1 motifs, or dCas9-KRAB/p300 to silence or activate specific enhancers, and test whether the primed chromatin state (H3K27ac, H3K4me1, accessibility) and faster re-induction are lost. To test sufficiency, force AP-1 binding there with a synthetic recruiter and test whether memory is created without the stimulus.

rewrites.title: Single-cell multiome with lineage/history tracing of AP-1 activity
rewrites.description: Combine an AP-1 reporter or recorder (e.g., Cre-based or fluorescent timer under TRE elements) with scRNA/ATAC multiome to label cells that experienced AP-1 activity and follow them after rest. Test whether past AP-1 history predicts accessibility state and restimulation response in individual cells, separating cell-autonomous memory from population heterogeneity.

rewrites.title: Acute degron-based AP-1 depletion in different time windows
rewrites.description: Use dTAG/auxin degrons on FOS, JUN, or pioneer-like AP-1 factors to remove AP-1 during the initial stimulus, after it, or only during recall. If memory requires ongoing AP-1, removal after priming should erase it; if AP-1 is needed only to establish memory, removal at that point should have no effect.

rewrites.title: Transient stimulus with long-term chromatin accessibility tracking
rewrites.description: Give cells a brief pulse of a stimulus that activates AP-1 (e.g., TPA, a growth factor, or an inflammatory cue), then run time-resolved ATAC-seq and CUT&RUN for AP-1 factors (FOS, JUN) and histone marks (H3K27ac, H3K4me1) for days to weeks after signal removal. Memory would predict that a subset of AP-1 motif-containing enhancers stays open or marked after AP-1 returns to baseline.

rewrites.title: Perturbing chromatin cofactors and testing memory in vivo
rewrites.description: Test whether AP-1 memory depends on partner factors such as BAF/SWI-SNF, p300, or pioneer factors by inhibiting or depleting them after the initial stimulus, and use CUT&Tag and Micro-C to track enhancer-promoter contacts. Validate in vivo, for example with repeated skin injury or inflammatory challenge, using lineage tracing and comparison of primary and secondary responses.

rewrites.title: Enhancer-level epigenetic readout and engineered AP-1 sites
rewrites.description: Map H3K27ac, H3K4me1, DNA methylation, and nucleosome remodeling (BAF) at AP-1-bound enhancers before, after, and long after stimulation. Then use dCas9 or motif mutation to delete or insert AP-1 sites at selected enhancers to test whether AP-1 binding is necessary and sufficient to leave a persistent open, primed state.

rewrites.title: Longitudinal chromatin accessibility after transient stimulus
rewrites.description: Stimulate cells (e.g., with TNF, wounding cues, or EGF), then perform ATAC-seq and CUT&Tag for AP-1 factors (FOS, JUN) and H3K27ac at multiple time points after withdrawal, including weeks later. AP-1 motif-containing open regions that outlast the stimulus and are absent in naive cells would indicate an epigenetic memory footprint.
